cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && python -c "
import boto3, json, re
s3 = boto3.client('s3')
resp = s3.list_objects_v2(Bucket='opal-data-harvest', Prefix='scores/v1/')
keys = [o['Key'] for o in resp.get('Contents', []) if re.search(r'/\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\.json$', o['Key'])]
missing_field_absent = True
for k in keys[:5]:
    doc = json.loads(s3.get_object(Bucket='opal-data-harvest', Key=k)['Body'].read())
    for field in ('robustness', 'peers_v'):
        rec = doc.get(field) or {}
        if rec.get('state') == 'MEASURED' and rec.get('value') in (None, ''):
            missing_field_absent = False
print('planted_negative_holds', missing_field_absent)
"

mutant.description: A naive slash-counting heuristic (classify a key as date-partitioned if it has exactly 3 '/' characters) was tried FIRST as a shortcut for AC1's own denominator check, before being caught and replaced with a per-key existence check and, in the criteria themselves, a proper date-suffix regex.
mutant.expected: The naive heuristic should be shown to misclassify at least one real object, proving it is an unsound instrument before being discarded in favour of the regex/per-key methods actually used in this instance's recorded invocations.
mutant.observed: The naive count("/")==3 heuristic misclassified BOTH slash-bearing keys (BP/_LN_Equity, NG/_LN_Equity) as 'missing a date-partitioned object' when in fact both had one (at count("/")==4, since the security key itself contains an internal slash) -- confirmed by a direct per-key list_objects_v2 call finding both objects present. This is the exact key-shape trap class row S141/AMGT-rk-23 already caught once this round on a different surface. The heuristic was discarded; the regex-based and per-key methods in this instance's own AC1/AC2/AC3 invocations do not share this flaw.
